issues.display_title: Issue #115: Stitch 360: new step-by-step flow — build one 360 panorama at a time
issues.main_description_html:
Demo by developer

2026-07-24.22-09-52.mp4

Summary

Stitch 360 has been fully redesigned. It used to work in batch mode (pick one folder → process many panoramas at once). It's now a step-by-step wizard focused on building one panorama at a time — much easier to follow, including for non-technical users.

New flow (4 steps)

  1. Photos — pick the shots from a single tripod position. The photos now show up as real previews (not blank boxes).
  2. Lens — the camera & lens are auto-detected from the photos; just confirm.
  3. Stitch — runs with a progress bar.
  4. Review & fix — see the finished panorama right away. If something looks off, a guide — "something look off? tell me what you see" — points to the fix.

What's better

  • Auto camera detection — no more guessing the lens manually.
  • Real previews — both the input photos and the stitched result show on screen.
  • Fix-it guide for imperfect results (e.g. a black gap or streaky colors), in plain language instead of technical terms.
  • Cleaner UI — consistent across every step, looks good in both light and dark mode.

Notes

  • Default output size is 8K to stay safe (avoids running out of memory).
  • Some advanced options turn on automatically when the stitching engine is on the newer version.

issues.display_title: Issue #90: Restructure the app's internal editing-tools data store for maintainability
issues.main_description_html:
Third step in the ongoing front-end cleanup effort (builds on G0 code quality setup and G1 data-handling upgrade).

Goals:

  • Eliminate the repeated outputDirectory<Tool> / logProcess<Tool> / <tool>CreateNewFile naming families (15 near-identical fields differing only by tool-name suffix).
  • Make each Edit tool's state independently readable/maintainable — isolated from the other 15 tools instead of tangled in one shared object.
  • Zero UX/behavior change — pure internal restructuring.

What changed:

  • src/renderer/features/edit/editSlice.ts — the old single file (735 lines, 91 reducers) holding state for all 16 Edit tools combined. Deleted — fully emptied after migration.
  • Added one self-contained file per tool: src/renderer/features/edit/<tool>/<tool>Slice.ts (crop, enfuse, imageResize, minifyJpg, scaleUpImage, autoLevel, equirectangularToCube, cubeToEquirectangular, imageStraightener, nadirBuilder, logoPatching, nadirPatching, stitching, roomStaging, virtualStaging2D) + a shared editShared/editSharedSlice.ts for cross-tool fields.
  • src/renderer/features/edit/editReducer.ts — now a plain Redux Toolkit combineReducers composing all 15 tool slices (previously a hand-written transitional reducer needed during the migration).
  • src/types/edit.ts — one typed state shape per tool (e.g. CropEditState, StitchingEditState) replacing the single flat EditState.
  • ~40 component/hook files across src/renderer/components/features/Edit/** updated to read/dispatch from each tool's own slice instead of the shared file.

What changed for users: Nothing — entirely behind-the-scenes. No visual or functional changes.

Why it matters: Each editing tool can now be understood, tested, and modified in isolation. Removes the naming-collision risk that made past cross-tool bugs easier to introduce.

Part of the larger front-end refactor initiative. Branch: feat/renderer-refactor-g3.

issues.display_title: Issue #82: [Bug] Selection lost when switching between Preview and Edit mode

Bug Report

Summary
When switching from Preview → Edit or Edit → Preview, files that appear visually selected (blue highlight) in the file browser are not actually selected. The Upload button shows 0 File(s) instead of the expected count.

Selection state persists across mode switches. Upload button reflects correct selected file count.

Actual Behavior

Visual selection (blue highlight) appears active but selection state is reset/lost. Upload count = 0.

Affected Area

  • File browser selection state
  • Mode switcher (Preview ↔ Edit toggle)
  • Upload button file count display

Notes

  • Selection highlight is purely visual — underlying selection state is cleared on mode switch
  • Likely a Redux slice or component re-mount issue where selection state is not preserved when switching modes

issues.display_title: Issue #88: File Manager: delete confirmation still uses native OS dialog instead of HeroUI modal
issues.main_description_html:
Summary

Deleting files/folders from the File Manager still opens a native OS message dialog ("Confirm — Delete the selected items?" / Cancel · Remove) instead of the app's HeroUI modal. Preview and Edit already use the HeroUI ConfirmDeleteModal, so the same destructive action looks and behaves differently depending on where it is triggered from.

Steps to Reproduce

  1. Open the File Manager (dual-pane browser)
  2. Select one or more files (or a folder)
  3. Click the trash icon / press Delete
  4. Observe the confirmation dialog

Expected Behavior

  • Confirmation uses ConfirmDeleteModal (HeroUI Modal), matching Preview and Edit
  • Same theme, typography, button styling and placement as the rest of the app
  • Text goes through i18next (t_confirm_delete_modal.*), so it is translated
  • "Don't ask again for this session" checkbox is available, like the renderer modal

Actual Behavior

  • A native OS dialog appears (macOS/Windows system styling), ignoring app theme
  • Title and message are hardcoded English strings in Rust — not translated
  • No "don't ask again" checkbox
  • Blocks the UI thread while open

Root Cause

The confirmation is raised in the backend, not the renderer:

  • src-tauri/src/commands/fs_ops.rs:399 — confirm_remove() calls app.dialog().message(...).blocking_show() via tauri_plugin_dialog
  • Callers:
    • fs_ops.rs:419 — delete_sources ("Delete the selected items?")
    • fs_ops.rs:462 — remove_images ("Delete the selected items?")
    • fs_ops.rs:502 — delete_folder ("Remove the selected folder?")

The renderer already has the correct component at src/renderer/components/modals/ConfirmDeleteModal.tsx (HeroUI Modal + pendingDelete state in filesSlice + performPendingDelete), used by Preview / Edit / ToolsImageSection. The File Manager delete path bypasses it and hits the Rust commands directly, which then raise their own dialog.

Note: remove_images core is also driven by the native context menu (AppHandle-only path), so removing the Rust dialog needs that path considered too — otherwise a right-click → Delete would get no confirmation at all.

Proposed Fix

  1. Route File Manager delete through the existing setPendingDelete → ConfirmDeleteModal → performPendingDelete flow (same as Preview/Edit)
  2. Have the renderer always pass disableRemoveWarning = true once the user has confirmed in the modal, so confirm_remove() short-circuits
  3. Decide what the native context-menu path should do — either emit an event to the renderer to open the HeroUI modal, or keep the native dialog only for that entry point
  4. Once no caller relies on it, delete confirm_remove() from fs_ops.rs

Affected Area

  • src-tauri/src/commands/fs_ops.rs (confirm_remove, delete_sources, remove_images, delete_folder)
  • src/renderer/components/modals/ConfirmDeleteModal.tsx
  • src/renderer/features/files/filesSlice.ts (pendingDelete), deleteConfirm.ts
  • File Manager delete trigger (trash icon / keyboard shortcut / native context menu)

Notes

  • Consistency only — deletes still go to the OS recycle bin via the trash crate, no change to destructive behavior
  • Confirmation must not be dropped in any path (see native context menu above)

issues.display_title: Issue #89: [Bug] Video restarts from 0:00 when entering fullscreen instead of continuing playback
issues.main_description_html:
Bug Report

Summary
While a video is playing in Preview, entering (or leaving) fullscreen restarts playback from 00:00 instead of continuing from the current position. Playback position, and any buffering already done, are lost on every fullscreen toggle.

Steps to Reproduce

  1. Open Preview and select a video file
  2. Let it play for a while (e.g. 30 seconds in)
  3. Toggle fullscreen / full-width on the viewer
  4. Observe the video

Expected Behavior

  • Video keeps playing uninterrupted across the fullscreen toggle
  • currentTime is preserved — playback continues from where it was
  • Play/pause state, volume and mute are preserved
  • No re-buffering from scratch

Actual Behavior

  • Video jumps back to 0:00 and starts over
  • Buffering spinner appears again as the source is re-fetched
  • Same on the way back out of fullscreen

Suspected Cause (not yet confirmed)

The playing video is not a <video> element in JSX — it is created imperatively in PanoramaViewer.tsx:

  • src/renderer/components/features/Preview/PanoramaViewer.tsx:386-439 — a useEffect does document.createElement('video'), sets src/autoplay/loop, calls video.play(), and stores it in videoRef + videoElement state
  • Its cleanup runs video.pause(); video.src = ''; video.load(); and nulls the refs — so any re-run of that effect destroys and rebuilds the element, which resets currentTime to 0
  • The element is then re-parented into the DOM by VideoContainer (PanoramaViewer.tsx:136-147) via appendChild / removeChild

Fullscreen is a Redux flag, layout.isPanoramaFullWidth, toggled at PanoramaViewer.tsx:908 and Content.tsx:283. If flipping it causes PanoramaViewer (or the subtree holding it) to unmount/remount — or otherwise re-runs that effect — the video element is recreated from scratch, matching the symptom exactly.

Worth checking as part of the investigation:

  • Whether PanoramaViewer actually unmounts on the toggle, or only re-renders
  • Content.tsx:400-408 — layout.isPanoramaFullWidth is in that effect's dependency array, so the flag already re-runs effects elsewhere on toggle
  • VideoContainer's appendChild/removeChild re-parenting: moving a <video> between containers can itself interrupt playback in some engines, even when the element survives

Affected Area

  • src/renderer/components/features/Preview/PanoramaViewer.tsx (video effect, VideoContainer, fullscreen toggle button)
  • src/renderer/components/core/Content.tsx (fullscreen toggle + effect deps)
  • src/renderer/features/layout/layoutSlice.ts (isPanoramaFullWidth)

Notes

  • Applies to both flat and 360 video playback — both go through the same imperative <video> element
  • If the element genuinely has to be recreated, the fallback is to save currentTime / paused state before teardown and restore it after — but keeping the same element alive across the toggle is the better fix

issues.display_title: Issue #97: Image Resize distorts rotation for photos with EXIF orientation
issues.main_description_html:
What happens

Resizing a photo with EXIF orientation 6 or 8 (portrait/rotated) through Edit → Image Resize produces a distorted, wrongly-rotated output. Orientation-1 photos are unaffected.

Root cause, two parts — both in do_resize / copy_metadata in src-tauri/src/commands/image_resize.rs:

  1. Resize doesn't apply EXIF orientation before resizing. Renderer sends targetWidth/targetHeight computed from display dimensions (orientation-corrected, width/height swapped for 6/8 — see files.rs:261-265). image::ImageReader::decode() reads raw sensor-orientation pixels (the image crate does not auto-apply EXIF orientation). resize_exact(target_w, target_h, ...) then force-stretches the raw (unswapped) pixels into the swapped target dims → wrong aspect ratio.
  2. The Orientation tag "strip" was a no-op. The fix for (1) bakes the rotation into the pixels before resizing, so the copied EXIF Orientation tag must be reset to 1 afterward or a viewer re-rotates the now-correct pixels a second time. The original attempt used -Orientation-=, which does nothing for a scalar (non-List) exiftool tag with no value — verified directly against the bundled exiftool binary ("0 image files updated", tag unchanged). rotate.rs had the exact same -Orientation-= pattern (and the same latent bug) for its own EXIF-reset step.

How to reproduce

  1. Take/use a JPEG with EXIF orientation 6 or 8 (portrait shot on a phone held in landscape, etc.)
  2. Open Edit → Image Resize, resize it
  3. Compare output rotation/aspect to source — distorted vs. expected

Found while running the pre-merge test plan (docs/refactor/pre-merge-test-plan.md §4.5, row E-3 Image Resize).

Fix

Fixed in 7cc5da9:

  • image_resize.rs: apply the EXIF orientation transform to the decoded pixels (apply_orientation, same table as rotate.rs) before resize_exact.
  • image_resize.rs and rotate.rs: swap -Orientation-= → -Orientation#=1 (raw numeric assign, bypasses the PrintConv string match a plain =1 also gets wrong) when copying metadata, so the tag is actually reset instead of silently surviving.

Goal

Resize (and Rotate) should preserve/produce the correct visual orientation and aspect ratio for every EXIF orientation value, not just 1.

DEMO FROM DEVELOPER

issues.display_title: Issue #102: Optimize Auto Level: adding files to the queue is slow
issues.main_description_html:
What happens

Edit → Auto Level: selecting files and adding them to the queue takes noticeably long before anything shows up in the list, especially for large panoramas.

Root cause: adding to the queue isn't just listing files — useAutoLevel.tsx's processFilesToAdd calls ipc.getPanoLevelMetadata per file (useAutoLevel.tsx:130), which runs full horizon/vanishing-point detection (pano_level::estimate_metadata) synchronously, and Promise.all (useAutoLevel.tsx:149) holds the whole batch back from appearing until every file finishes.

That detection call was paying for more decode work than it needs, in src-tauri/src/pano_level/mod.rs / image_io.rs:

  1. read_rgb always did a full-resolution decode, even though line detection only ever looks at a 1024px-wide analysis image (detect::make_analysis_image downsamples right after).
  2. The equirectangular-ratio guard ran after that full decode, so a clearly-non-panorama file still paid for the full decode before being rejected.

How to reproduce

  1. Open Edit → Auto Level
  2. Select several images (especially large/high-res ones) and add them to the queue
  3. Notice the delay before items appear in the queue list

Fix

Fixed in the working tree (not yet committed):

  • Check the equirectangular ratio from the file header (imagesize::size, no decode) before decoding anything — a non-pano file is rejected instantly.
  • Added image_io::read_rgb_scaled, reusing the same reduced-DCT-scale JPEG decode already used for grid thumbnails (commands::image::decode_jpeg_scaled, made pub(crate)). The dry-run path (estimate_metadata, used for the add-to-queue preview) now decodes at analysis resolution instead of full resolution — up to ~64x less decode work on a large panorama. The real leveling run (level_panorama) still decodes full-res, since it needs to write the corrected output.

cargo check clean, all 20 pano_level unit tests pass.

Goal

Adding files to the Auto Level queue should feel roughly as fast as the other Edit subfeatures (Crop, Enfuse, Resize) — proportional to file count, not to how large each source image is.

Test plan reference

docs/refactor/pre-merge-test-plan.md §4.5, row E-6 Auto Level.

issues.display_title: Issue #112: Multiview grid collapses into narrow strips while images load
issues.main_description_html:
Demo by developer

Image Issue

What happens

Selecting more than one file switches the viewer to MultiView. Before the images finish
decoding, every cell holds nothing but a spinner — and the grid columns shrink to that
spinner's width, so the whole grid renders as a row of thin vertical strips in the middle of
the viewer. Once the images arrive the columns snap out to full size.

The numbered badges stay at their normal size throughout, which makes the strips look even
narrower than they are.

How to reproduce

  1. Open Preview on a folder of panoramas
  2. Ctrl+click several files (the more, the more visible)
  3. Watch the viewer for the moment between the mode switch and the images appearing

Goal

The grid should hold its size while the images load — the cells reserve their space and the
spinner sits inside it, instead of the layout jumping once decoding finishes.

Notes

Not caused by the renderer refactor. The same markup is in the Electron build
(src/renderer/components/features/Preview/Main.tsx:702) and behaves the same way.

Cause: the multiview grid is shrink-to-fit inside a centering flex column, so the column width
comes from the cell content. The cells set min-h-[150px] but no matching min-w, so while
only the spinner is rendered there is nothing to give the column any width.

Found while running the pre-merge test plan (docs/refactor/pre-merge-test-plan.md, scenario P5).

issues.display_title: Issue #113: Full width has no visible way out for images and panoramas
issues.main_description_html:
Demo by developer

What happens

Full width is an immersive mode: it hides the header, the title bar and the browse panel. The
button that turns it on lives in the browse panel's footer — so switching it on hides the only
control that can switch it back off.

For a video this is not visible, because the video overlay carries its own minimize button. For
a still image or a panorama there is no on-screen control left at all. The only way back is the
Escape key, and nothing on screen says so.

How to reproduce

  1. Open Preview on a folder of panoramas and select a still image
  2. Turn on full width (the window icon in the browse panel footer, or its shortcut)
  3. Look for a way back — the header, the title bar and the browse panel are all gone, and no
    button in the viewer exits the mode

Goal

Full width should keep one visible way out, the way map full screen already does — it renders a
dedicated exit button in the corner of the viewer while it is active.

Notes

Not caused by the renderer refactor. The Electron build hides the header the same way
(src/renderer/components/layouts/Header/Header.tsx:307) and has the same gap.

Hiding the header itself is intended and worth keeping. What is missing is the exit affordance
for the non-video case.

Found while running the pre-merge test plan (docs/refactor/pre-merge-test-plan.md, scenario P7).

issues.display_title: Issue #114: Rename input is cut off by the row below it in the browse grid
issues.main_description_html:
Image Issue

What happens

Renaming a file in the browse grid opens a textarea that is taller than the label slot, so it
overflows downward on purpose — long names need the room. But the card in the row below is
painted over it, cutting the textarea off partway down. The bottom of the input, and any text
that wrapped into it, sits behind the next row's thumbnail.

Affects every browse grid: Preview, Edit and File Manager.

How to reproduce

  1. Open Preview on a folder with at least two rows of files
  2. Select a file in the first row, then click its name to start a rename
  3. The textarea opens over the row below — its lower half is covered by the next row's thumbnail

Goal

The rename textarea stays fully visible over whatever is beneath it, the way it does in the
Electron build.

Notes

Not caused by the renderer refactor — development renders the grid the same way.

Cause: each virtualized row is positioned with a transform
(src/renderer/components/shared/browse/BrowseGridRows.tsx), which gives every row its own
stacking context. The z-20 the card already sets while renaming
(src/renderer/components/shared/browse/BrowseCards.tsx) therefore only competes inside its own
row; between rows the later one in the DOM wins. Electron did not virtualize this grid, so every
card shared one stacking context and the z-index was enough.

Found while running the pre-merge test plan (docs/refactor/pre-merge-test-plan.md, scenario P11).

the upload progress panel never appears in Edit's browse panel — the area between Quick Access
and the footer stays empty for the whole upload. Switching to Preview shows the panel with the
correct progress, so the upload itself is fine; only Edit is missing the display.

How to reproduce

  1. Open the Edit viewer
  2. Select a few 360 images → Upload → GoThru (Panorra and Street View behave the same)
  3. Start the upload and watch the left browse panel

Nothing renders between Quick Access and the footer.

  1. Switch to Preview — the "Uploading to GoThru (n/N)" accordion is there.

Goal

Edit's browse panel shows the same upload progress panel as Preview, for all three upload targets.

Notes

<UploadInfo /> is only mounted in Preview/Browse.tsx:379. Edit/Browse.tsx imports
FooterInfo and QuickAccess from ../Preview/ but not UploadInfo, so the upload state has
nowhere to render while Edit is open.

The IPC path is intact — Rust upload-progress → ipcHandlers/upload.ts → addProcessingFile →
state.files.processingFiles all work; only the mount is missing.

Not caused by the renderer refactor: UploadInfo has only ever been referenced from
Preview/Browse.tsx in this repo's history.

FileManager/Browse.tsx also lacks it, and is deliberately left alone — it is a dual-panel view
and which panel should host the upload info has not been decided.

Fix on feat/renderer-refactor-g0: import and mount <UploadInfo /> above <FooterInfo /> in
Edit/Browse.tsx, wrapped in the same background container Preview uses.

Found while running the pre-merge test plan (docs/refactor/pre-merge-test-plan.md, scenario U3).

issues.display_title: Issue #104: Opening a folder from search results goes nowhere
issues.main_description_html:
What happens

Search in Preview or Edit walks the whole folder tree, so the results can include folders that
sit several levels below the folder you are in. Double-clicking one of those does not open it —
a "folder not found" warning appears and the listing stays where it was.

If the folder happens to be a direct child of the current folder, it does open, but the search
box stays filled, so the search immediately runs again inside the new folder. You never see the
folder's actual contents, only search results again.

File Manager does not have this problem — only Preview and Edit.

How to reproduce

  1. Open Preview on a folder that has a subfolder, which itself contains another folder
  2. Open the header search, leave the recursive toggle on
  3. Type part of the name of that deepest folder
  4. Double-click it in the results
  5. A warning appears, nothing opens

Then:

  1. Search for a folder that is a direct child of the current folder
  2. Double-click it → it opens, but the search box is still filled and the listing shows search
    results instead of the folder contents

Same in Edit.

Goal

A folder in the search results should open that exact folder, wherever it lives, and the search
should end there — the listing shows the folder's normal contents, as it does in File Manager.

Notes

Not caused by the renderer refactor — same code on development. Dates back to when recursive
search was added (June); the handling was only written for File Manager, and Preview/Edit were
missed. Found while running the pre-merge test plan
(docs/refactor/pre-merge-test-plan.md, scenario H7).

issues.display_title: Issue #108: Videos show as broken images in the multiview grid
issues.main_description_html:
Image Issue

What happens

Selecting more than one file opens the multiview grid. Any video in that selection does not
render — its cell shows a broken image and the file name instead of the video.

The same videos render correctly in the browse grid on the left, so it is only the multiview
that cannot show them.

There is a second half to it: if the file being displayed happens to be a video, the whole
multiview grid disappears and the viewer switches to the single video player, even though
several files are still selected.

How to reproduce

  1. Open Preview on a folder holding both images and videos
  2. Select one image and two videos (ctrl+click)
  3. The multiview grid opens — the two video cells show a broken image with the file name

Then:

  1. Click the video card in the grid on the left, so the video becomes the displayed file
  2. The multiview grid disappears entirely and only the video player is left

Goal

A video in the multiview grid should show its own video frame, the way it already does in the
browse grid, and the grid should stay on screen for as long as several files are selected,
whichever one of them is currently displayed.

The card should not look clickable either. Multiview cells have no click behaviour, so the play
badge the card inherited from the browse thumbnail promises something that never happens — it
should mark the file as a video without inviting a click.

Notes

Not caused by the renderer refactor — the same markup is on development. The grid draws every
selected file as an image, and an image element cannot decode a video.

Found while running the pre-merge test plan (docs/refactor/pre-merge-test-plan.md, scenario P1).

issues.display_title: Issue #103: Typing a wrong path throws you out to "My Computer" with no message
issues.main_description_html:
What happens

Type a folder path that doesn't exist into the path bar and press Enter (or click Apply), and
the app silently dumps you at the "My Computer" drive list. The folder you were working in is
gone from view, with no message explaining why.

The same thing happens without any typing: if a folder you have open gets renamed, moved, or
sits on a drive you unplug, the app throws you back to the drive list a few seconds later —
again with no explanation.

How to reproduce

  1. Open any folder in Preview (also happens in Edit and File Manager)
  2. Click the pencil icon in the path bar to edit the path
  3. Add some junk to the end of the path so it points nowhere, e.g. ...\panoramas\360 - Office
    → ...\panoramas\360 - Officeasdasd
  4. Press Enter, or click Apply
  5. The grid empties and you land on the "My Computer" drive list (C:, D:, …)

Goal

A wrong path should not cost you your place. Tell the user what went wrong and leave them where
they were:

  • Typing a path that doesn't exist should show a message and keep the current folder open, with
    the path still editable so the typo can be corrected.
  • A folder that disappears mid-session (renamed, moved, drive unplugged) should show a message
    and leave the listing on screen, so the drive can be reconnected or the folder renamed back
    without losing your place.
  • Whatever the fix, it should behave the same in Preview, Edit and File Manager — they share the
    same folder-watching logic.

issues.display_title: Issue #105: The signed-in account can be removed from the upload account list
issues.main_description_html:
Image Issue

What happens

In the upload account list (Upload to GoThru), the account the app itself is signed in with
shows a remove (×) button, so it can be deleted from the list like any other account. It is
supposed to have no remove button at all.

How to reproduce

  1. Sign in to the app with account A
  2. Select some images and open Upload → GoThru
  3. Add New Account and sign in — with account B, or with account A again
  4. Reopen the upload panel

Account A now carries a remove button next to it.

It does not happen on a fresh sign-in; it starts once the stored sign-in has been renewed —
signing the same email in again from the upload modal is the quickest way to see it.

Goal

The account the app is signed in with should never offer a remove button in the upload account
list. The only way to sign out of it stays where it already is, in the user menu. Other accounts
added for uploading keep their remove button.

Notes

Not caused by the renderer refactor — the same code is on development and in the old Electron
app (ListAccounts.tsx:459). The list hides the button by comparing tokens, but a token is not a
stable identity: every sign-in issues a new one, and signing in from the upload modal replaces the
stored token while the app's own copy stays behind, after which the two never match again.

Found while running the pre-merge test plan (docs/refactor/pre-merge-test-plan.md, scenario H9).

issues.display_title: Issue #106: Full-screen modal footer is clipped in windowed mode ("Click here to learn more" cut off)
issues.main_description_html:
What happens

Upload → Upload to GoThru (and every other full-screen modal): the footer is clipped at the bottom of the window. The description line is visible, but the "Click here to learn more" link underneath it is cut off — only the top few pixels of the text render.

Reproduces in a windowed app; in OS fullscreen the footer is fine.

Root cause: HeroUI's size="full" modal hardcodes h-[100dvh] on the wrapper slot and h-[100dvh] min-h-[100dvh] on the base slot (@heroui/theme modal.js → modal tv slots). The app renders a custom 32px titlebar and offsets the modal below it via .titlebar-safe-modal-wrapper (index.css:141), which only set top: var(--menubar-h) / bottom: 0:

  1. The wrapper has an explicit height: 100dvh, so bottom: 0 is ignored — the wrapper stays a full viewport tall while starting 32px lower, spilling exactly --menubar-h past the window bottom.
  2. The base's min-h-[100dvh] beats any max-height clamp, so shrinking the child alone doesn't help either.

--menubar-h is 32px windowed and 0px in fullscreen (TitleBar.tsx:44) — which is why the bug only shows up windowed, and why the clipped strip is exactly one titlebar tall.

How to reproduce

  1. Run the app windowed (not OS fullscreen)
  2. Select an image → Upload → GoThru, log in so the full-screen upload view shows
  3. Look at the footer: "Click here to learn more" is cut off by the window bottom edge

Fix

Fixed in the working tree (not yet committed), CSS only, in src/renderer/index.css:

.titlebar-safe-modal-wrapper {
  top: var(--menubar-h, 0px) !important;
  bottom: 0 !important;
  height: calc(100dvh - var(--menubar-h, 0px)) !important;
}

.titlebar-safe-modal-wrapper > * {
  height: 100% !important;
  min-height: 0 !important;
  max-height: 100% !important;
}

Shrinks the wrapper by the titlebar height and clears the base's min-height so the modal fits inside it. One rule fixes all four full-size modals that share this wrapper — GoThru, StreetView, Panorra, and the Help modal — instead of patching each one.

Side effect (intended): the height math in GridThumbnails.tsx, GoThru/Upload.tsx, Panorra/Upload.tsx and StreetView/Publish.tsx, which measures upload-modal-wrapper / upload-modal-footer clientHeight, now reads the corrected heights.

Goal

The full-screen modal footer must be fully visible in windowed mode — the "Click here to learn more" link clickable, no content hidden behind the window edge — matching the Electron app's layout.

Test plan reference

docs/refactor/pre-merge-test-plan.md §4 — Upload group (GoThru / StreetView / Panorra) plus the Help modal.
